groups.title: Gauge two-point functions AA
groups.summary: The one-loop self-energies of the gluon, W and B fields (20 graphs, superficial degree 2) fix the gauge field constants δZA(r), equal to 113gs2, 116g2 and −4318g′2 in units of 116π21ϵ. Gauge, ghost and Higgs loops give the d-dimensional transverse tensor; fermion loops give its barred form and an evanescent, non-transverse remainder g‾μν⁢pˆ2, the two-point parts of the evanescent counterterms E˜F(r) and EA(r). Mixed pairs of gauge factors have no pole.

groups.title: Gauge three-point functions AAA
groups.summary: The three-gauge functions (54 graphs, superficial degree 1) have a pole only for three gluons and three W fields. The bosonic loops multiply the d-dimensional tree vertex, the fermion loops its barred form with the coefficient 23⁢S(r); the result fixes the vertex factor δZcr+32δZA(r), equal to 23gs2 and −16g2 in units of 116π21ϵ, and gives the three-point part of E˜F(r) with the same coefficient as the two-point function.
groups.count_note: The report counts 54 graphs; the run has 3 more in W W W, graphs that vanish by group theory; the report's enumeration ran on one representative component tuple per assignment and did not generate them, and their values vanish.

groups.title: Gauge four-point functions AAAA
groups.summary: The four-gauge functions at zero momentum (237 graphs, superficial degree 0) have a pole only for four gluons and four W fields, a combination of the d-dimensional and the barred quartic tree vertex. They fix the factor 2⁢δZA(r)+2⁢δZcr (−73gs2 and −136g2 in units of 116π21ϵ) and confirm that one field constant and one coupling constant per factor fit the two-, three- and four-point functions.
groups.count_note: The report counts 237 graphs; the run has 9 more in W W W B, graphs that vanish by group theory; the report's enumeration ran on one representative component tuple per assignment and did not generate them, and their values vanish.

groups.title: Fermion two-point functions Ψ̄Ψ
groups.summary: The self-energies of the five fermion multiplets (16 graphs, superficial degree 1, gauge and Yukawa bubbles) have the pole 116π21ϵ⁢(Cf+𝒴f)⁢/p‾Pcf, four-dimensional and without evanescent part. They fix the fermion field constants δZf=−116π21ϵ⁢(Cf+𝒴f), with Cf the Casimir and 𝒴f the Yukawa part of the multiplet; only the physical component is renormalised.

groups.title: Fermion–gauge vertices Ψ̄ΨA
groups.summary: The fermion–gauge vertices of the ten pairs of a multiplet and a gauge factor acting on it (46 graphs, superficial degree 0) have a pole proportional to the tree vertex γ‾μPcf𝒯fa, with the factor 116π21ϵ⁢(Cf+Cad(r)+𝒴f) and no evanescent part. Together with the fermion self-energies they fix the coupling constants through the cross-class condition that the vertex and kinetic coefficients differ by −Cad(r).

groups.title: Higgs two-point function H†H
groups.summary: The Higgs self-energy (8 graphs, superficial degree 2) fixes δZH=116π21ϵ⁢(−Y˜+2⁢CH) and δm2=116π21ϵ⁢m2⁢(6⁢λ+Y˜−3⁢CH), with Y˜=3⁢yu2+3⁢yd2+ye2. The Yukawa fermion loops give the barred and hatted structure Y˜⁢(23⁢pˆ2+p‾2) instead of the d-dimensional p2; the difference is the two-point part of the evanescent counterterms E˜H and EH.

groups.title: Higgs–gauge functions H†HA and H†HAA
groups.summary: The scalar–gauge vertices with one and two gauge fields (146 graphs, superficial degrees 1 and 0) have bosonic poles with the d-dimensional tree structure and Yukawa-loop poles with its barred form. They fix the vertex factors 116π21ϵ⁢(−Y˜+2⁢CH−Cad(r)) and 116π21ϵ⁢(−Y˜+2⁢CH−Cad(r)−Cad(s)) and give the three- and four-point parts of E˜H; the functions with an external gluon have no pole.
groups.count_note: The report counts 146 graphs; the run has 1 more in W H H†, graphs that vanish by group theory; the report's enumeration ran on one representative component tuple per assignment and did not generate them, and their values vanish.

groups.title: Higgs four-point function (H†H)²
groups.summary: The quartic Higgs function at zero momentum (63 graphs, superficial degree 0) has a pole proportional to the tree vertex and fixes δλ=116π21ϵ⁢(2⁢λ⁢Y˜−6⁢λ⁢CH−Y4+3⁢G416+12⁢λ2), with Y4=3⁢yu4+3⁢yd4+ye4 and G4=2⁢g2⁢g′2+3⁢g4+g′4. The resulting beta function of λ is the known one-family value.

groups.title: Yukawa vertices Ψ̄ΨH
groups.summary: The six Yukawa vertices and their conjugates (32 graphs, superficial degree 0) have poles proportional to the tree vertices and fix the Yukawa counterterms δyk. The vertex factor is identical for a vertex and its conjugate, and the resulting beta functions of yu, yd, ye are the known one-family values.

groups.title: Ghost and BRST-source functions
groups.summary: The functions with a BRST source and ghosts (20 graphs; superficial degree 1 for ρω, 0 otherwise) fix the ghost field constant and the common coefficient −116π21ϵ⁢12Cad(r) of all non-linear source terms (116π21ϵ⁢12Cad(r) for the linear term of ρaμ); they vanish for the hypercharge. Functions with an external antighost follow from these by the ghost equation and are not computed separately.

groups.title: Breaking of ωA
groups.summary: The ghost–gauge two-point function with one breaking vertex (10 graphs, superficial degree 3) has the evanescent pole 116π21ϵ⁢13i⁢S(r)⁢qˆ2⁢q‾ν, cancelled by the variation of the evanescent counterterm EA(r). Its finite breaking, −116π2⁢13⁢S(r) times N3(r), fixes the longitudinal restoring coefficient rQL(r)=−S(r)3; there is no finite gauge-boson mass term.

groups.title: Breaking of ωAA and the anomaly
groups.summary: The functions with a ghost and two gauge fields (40 graphs, superficial degree 2) have an evanescent pole for gluons and W fields and a finite breaking that fixes the cubic restoring coefficient rQ3⁢f(r)=−S(r)3. Their parity-odd part is proportional to the anomaly traces Dabc, which vanish for the Standard-Model charges (anomaly).

groups.title: Breaking of ωAAA and ωAAAA
groups.summary: The functions with a ghost and three or four gauge fields (1320 graphs, superficial degrees 1 and 0) have no pole. The finite breaking of the four-point class fixes the thirteen quartic restoring coefficients; the five-point class has no finite breaking.
groups.count_note: The report counts 1320 graphs. It includes the 120 graphs of the external-field sets G G W W ω_W, W W W W ω_W and W W ω_W B B, which the automation does not treat as classes: no non-zero, Lorentz-invariant and rigidly invariant local monomial has these fields.

groups.title: Breaking of ωΨ̄Ψ
groups.summary: The ghost–fermion–antifermion functions (42 graphs, superficial degree 1), including graphs with the ghost of the breaking vertex on an internal line, have an evanescent pole 116π21ϵ⁢12Cad(r)⁢Δ1(fr), cancelled by the variation of the singular fermion source counterterm, and no four-dimensional pole. The finite breaking fixes the difference of the finite fermion–gauge and fermion-source coefficients (finite fermion counterterms).

groups.title: Breaking of ωΨ̄ΨA
groups.summary: The functions with a ghost, a fermion pair and a gauge field (220 graphs, superficial degree 0) have no pole. Their finite breaking is non-zero only for gluon and W ghosts, 116π2⁢14Cad(r) times a commutator structure, and confirms the finite source coefficient −14Cad(r).

groups.title: Breaking of ωH†H, ωH†HA and higher
groups.summary: The functions with a ghost and Higgs legs (525 graphs) have an evanescent pole only in ωH†H, 116π21ϵ⁢23Y˜⁢NˆH, cancelled by the variation of EH. The finite breaking of ωH†H and ωH†HA fixes the scalar–gauge restoring coefficients, all Yukawa combinations; the classes with two gauge fields or four scalars have no breaking.

groups.title: Breaking of ωΨ̄ΨH
groups.summary: The functions with a ghost, a fermion pair and a Higgs leg (122 graphs, superficial degree 0) have no pole. The finite breaking is non-zero only for the W ghost, 116π2⁢12g2 times Yukawa structures reproduced by the finite fermion source terms, and it has no component along the hypercharge ghost, which is required for the normalisation (N4) to admit a solution.

groups.title: Breaking with BRST sources: ωωR̄Ψ
groups.summary: The functions with two ghosts, a fermion source and a fermion (54 graphs, superficial degree 0) have no pole, N0=0, consistent with 𝐛dδS(1)=0 in this class, where the fermion and ghost source counterterms have the same singular coefficient. Their finite breaking fixes the finite fermion source coefficient rQRfr=−Cad(r)4. The other ghost-number-one functions with a BRST source have no one-loop graph with the breaking vertex, so the breaking vanishes there.
groups.count_note: The report and the run both count 54 graphs. The report also lists ω_W ω_W ω_W ζ_W (no graph), which is not a class of the run; the run has seven source classes without graphs that the report does not list.

groups.title: Breaking of the one-point function of the abelian ghost
groups.summary: This class is not one of the report's eighteen: the automation evaluates the one-point function of the hypercharge ghost ωB with one insertion of the breaking vertex (5 graphs), for which the report has no subsection. The automation finds no component of the finite breaking in this class.
groups.note: Not one of the report's eighteen classes: the run evaluates the ghost-number-one one-point function of the abelian ghost, with one insertion of the breaking, and the report has no subsection for it.

classes.summary: Green's function with one insertion of Δ1. Pole part: −𝐛dδS(1) restricted to these legs (pole identity). Finite breaking: the component of X1 on these legs (the projected coefficient of ηϵ). The pole is written after integration by parts, with no derivative on the ghost. Its four-dimensional part vanishes (checked numerically by the build): the pole is evanescent. Its finite breaking enters the restoring condition that fixes the finite coefficients of: Longitudinal two-point term of the gluon.

classes.summary: Green's function with one insertion of Δ1. Pole part: −𝐛dδS(1) restricted to these legs (pole identity). Finite breaking: the component of X1 on these legs (the projected coefficient of ηϵ). The pole is written after integration by parts, with no derivative on the ghost. Its four-dimensional part vanishes (checked numerically by the build): the pole is evanescent. The display does not apply the trace identities of three generators; its terms without a hatted object cancel only once these identities are used. Its finite breaking enters the restoring condition that fixes the finite coefficients of: Longitudinal two-point term of the SU(2) gauge field, Cubic SU(2) gauge vertex.

classes.summary: Green's function with one insertion of Δ1. Pole part: −𝐛dδS(1) restricted to these legs (pole identity). Finite breaking: the component of X1 on these legs (the projected coefficient of ηϵ). The pole is written after integration by parts, with no derivative on the ghost. Its four-dimensional part vanishes (checked numerically by the build): the pole is evanescent. Its finite breaking enters the restoring condition that fixes the finite coefficients of: Higgs–hypercharge current term.
